newsitem.title: UK: North Sea crude market firms with supply tight.
newsitem.headline: North Sea crude market firms with supply tight.

text.p: A lack of early February physical Brent availabilities underpinned a firm North Sea crude market on Thursday, traders said.
Two wet Brent deals on Wednesday at unconfirmed levels were widely heard at around parity to Feb Brent paper, valueing physical barrels at a premium of over 30 cents to March paper.
"There's nothing left in the (Feb) 1-8 bracket. It looks like there's no avails there," said one physical trader.
The one standard-sized Brent cargo nominated from the paper chains on Thursday, a Feb 7-9 loader, was heard to have been kept early by the equity holder.
Another 550,000 barrel cargo with the same loading dates could also go into the 15 day market, traders said.

March Brent paper was trading up nearly 30 cents a barrel at $22.75/$22.80 at 1303 GMT. Intermonth spreads firmed with Feb/Mar climbing to talk around +38/+45 cents. Mar/Apr traded at +46 and +47 cents.
Other North Sea grades were also assessed firm after Forties, Oseberg, Gulfaks C and Draugen all traded at higher levels on Thursday.
"Forties and Oseberg are committed well into the second decade...it's looking fairly bullish," a trader said.
Loadings of Norwegian Ekofisk cargoes scheduled under the January programme have been delayed by around five days with the last January cargo given Feb 5-7 dates.
But traders said there were no cancellations from the original programme after a gas leak in a pipeline shut in production at the 350,000 barrel per day field for a week.
First loadings under the February programme, due to be released on Friday, are expected towards the end of the first decade of the month.
In the Mediterranean, Urals buying interest remained subdued.
